references_named: Stanley Brouwn, the distance / step works
Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: The work is a strong, restrained Brouwn readymade: pointer deltas converted to real metres via the CSS reference pixel, never drawn, never stored. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1), the chance/order axis is legible (deterministic rule, aimless journey), and the tone is dry and witty without being preachy. However, G6 fails: 'this way browser' is already catalogued in the corpus with the identical mechanism (pointermove deltas, CSS reference pixel, no rendering/storage/network) and the identical Brouwn/Benjamin references. The candidate is a duplicate of the existing entry, not a materially distinct work.
reservations: G6 duplicate of the existing 'this way browser (2026)' catalogue entry — same source, same mechanism, same references, same argument. Even with a refined motivation.md, the work itself is the same object.
revision_suggestion: Either retire this candidate as already-published, or materially differentiate it: e.g., add a second walker (multi-pointer sum), bind the measure to a specific Brouwn unit (his own step length) rather than an assumed 750mm, or stage the unreproducibility differently — perhaps by exposing the gap between assumed and actual pixel density as the visible artwork rather than only a number.
